d.As Áreas de Preservação Permanente são e: Permanent Preservation Areas are defined by law as areas that serve to preserve water resources, landscape and geological stability, protect biodiversity, the gene flow of fauna and flora and the soil, and ensure the protection and well-being of human populations. They should therefore be protected by keeping their native vegetation and not used for housing: besides causing many environmental impacts, these areas are fragile and prone to flooding and landslides, on top of the vulnerability and social segregation the families living there face.
d.Atualmente nas áreas urbanas é comum dep: In urban areas today it is common to find settlements near water bodies, in areas legally designated as Permanent Preservation Areas, which must be preserved because they are fundamental to the maintenance and balance of ecosystems and to socio-environmental quality. Although specific protective legislation exists, APPs suffer from misuse, especially in large urban centers, where disorderly urbanization and the resulting lack of decent housing lead people to occupy these spaces, endangering their own health and the conservation of these places.
d.Dado que o sombreamento urbano tem impac: Since urban shading directly affects quality of life, pedestrian comfort and climate change mitigation, this research project analyzes urban shading in Cuiabá-MT using the sky view factor (SVF), urban canyons, vertical growth and the urban tree index, analyzed by road hierarchy in the four administrative regions.

d.A constante exposição à umidade e intemp: Constant exposure to moisture and weather causes various fungal pathologies in interior and exterior building finishes. Indoors, continuous exposure can cause health problems; outdoors, it causes aesthetic deterioration of the building, requiring new investment to fix the damage. Developing antimicrobial surfaces is therefore highly significant and of great public interest. To address this, the project applies nanomaterials in antimicrobial paints for masonry and ceiling finishes. It proposes synthesizing zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO-NP) with different heat treatments (60, 400 and 550 °C). The synthesized nanoparticles and the paints will be characterized by physicochemical methods, and their antimicrobial activity against the 6 most common microorganisms in damp indoor and outdoor building environments will be assessed by microbiological tests. The physical properties and antifungal potential of paints with ZnO-NP will be evaluated, together with an environmental assessment by leaching test, checking whether zinc ions harmful to the environment are released. The results will show the feasibility of a new application of ZnO in surface coating polymers to make them self-sterilizing, benefiting the environment and society.
d.A crescente urbanização transforma cada: Growing urbanization increasingly transforms the local environment, replacing natural vegetation with built-up areas where concrete and asphalt create extensive impermeable surfaces. Land use and land cover change directly affects climate conditions, and the city starts to show the Urban Heat Island (UHI) phenomenon. Studies show the relevance of the topic and the need to characterize UHI to diagnose the current situation and find ways to mitigate it. Remote sensing makes it possible to extract Land Surface Temperature (LST), and remotely collected data characterize the Surface Urban Heat Island (SUHI). Alongside LST, several indices are analyzed to correlate with SUHI, among which Land Use and Land Cover (LULC) has gained prominence. In recent years, many studies have applied artificial intelligence, specifically machine learning and deep learning, to predict temperature and find ways to mitigate UHI. Although studies address LST prediction, the correlation between LULC and LST impacts remains little explored. The project therefore assesses the impact of LULC on UHI formation using an artificial intelligence approach, evaluating deep learning methods with artificial neural networks. Results will be assessed with accuracy validation metrics such as precision, sensitivity and F1-measure. The study area is Cuiabá-MT, and new locations will be added to test the model's ability to generalize under different climate conditions. The main contribution is to verify whether deep learning can optimize UHI characterization and to analyze the influence of LULC. Socially, it aims to produce information to support urban planning towards smarter, more sustainable cities.
d.A produção de cimento convencional é uma: Conventional cement production is one of the main sources of greenhouse gas emissions and intensive use of natural resources, a critical challenge for global environmental sustainability. Sustainable alternatives in construction, such as supplementary cementitious materials, are a promising way to reduce environmental impact and reuse waste. This project investigates the potential of corn straw ash (CPM), an abundant by-product of Mato Grosso's agribusiness, as a pozzolanic material to partially replace Portland cement in mortars and concretes. Although international literature recognizes agro-industrial ashes for similar uses, there is a significant gap in the study of CPM, especially methods using advanced characterization of pozzolanic activity, durability and thermal performance. The central problem is the environmental impact of cement production and the potential new uses of agro-industrial by-products. The hypothesis is that properly processed and characterized CPM has great potential as a pozzolanic material, meeting standards and giving mechanical and durability properties equal or superior to conventional cement, as well as better thermal comfort. Preliminary evidence shows that properly calcined agro-industrial ashes are highly reactive due to their high amorphous silica content. The method involves collecting corn straw, processing it by self-combustion and controlled burning at different temperatures, followed by chemical, physical, thermal, structural and morphological characterization. Mortars with different cement replacement levels (0, 10, 20 and 30%) will then be produced and tested for physical-mechanical performance, pozzolanic activity and durability against a control. The best burning method and replacement level will be used to produce concrete blocks, with further tests of thermal conductivity and transmittance to assess environmental comfort for urban use, combining the team's fields of expertise. The topic is aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals: Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure (SDG 9), Sustainable Cities and Communities (SDG 11), Responsible Consumption and Production (SDG 12) and Climate Action (SDG 13).
d.A proposta busca analisar a vulnerabilid: The proposal analyzes the climate vulnerability of the neighborhoods along the Barbado Stream in Cuiabá-MT, considering the impacts of climate change and urban pressures in the area. The 9.5 km stream crosses several neighborhoods and suffers environmental degradation from irregular settlements, inappropriate land use and extreme weather events. The study considers flood risk, earth movement, land use and local socioeconomic aspects. The method includes socioeconomic and environmental surveys, on-site analysis and satellite imagery to produce diagnostic maps, plus ENVI-met modeling. Urban interventions based on nature-based solutions (NbS) will then be proposed, in line with climate-sensitive planning and current legislation such as Cuiabá's Master Plan. The project aims to mitigate climate impacts, improve urban resilience and provide guidelines for revising urban and environmental legislation, while contributing to innovation and sustainability in Mato Grosso.
d.As cidades inteligentes surgem no contex: Smart cities emerged with computerization as a public management solution that uses information and communication technologies to interconnect public systems, measuring and monitoring their efficiency. This research project studies how smart cities can contribute to urban sustainability, improving future sustainability prospects and reducing the environmental damage caused so far. Methodologically, it is exploratory and qualitative, based on secondary data. It will carry out a case study of the seven municipalities in Brazil's Center-West region classified as smart cities (Brasília-DF, Campo Grande-MS, Goiânia-GO, Cuiabá-MT, Anápolis-GO, Lucas do Rio Verde-MT and Aparecida de Goiânia-GO), identifying how they manage space and resources and how they relate to the natural landscape. It also defines these concepts through a theoretical review supporting propositions on the relationship between smart cities and urban ecology. The hypothesis is that technology and innovation alone cannot produce a sustainable urban space, especially regarding ecology and the environment, but this form of governance can be a tool to achieve it, helping public authorities make sound urban management and planning decisions. The expected result is to present the factors that characterize smart and sustainable cities, linking them to ESG (Environmental, Social and Governance) principles for cities that are more socially just, less unequal and environmentally responsible.
d.As cidades, como as conhecemos, são espa: Cities, as we know them, are spaces of social and economic relations that are inherent to human beings, who depend on them to survive and develop. This research investigates the urban morphology of the new Mato Grosso towns consolidated from the 1980s onwards. Urban morphology is understood as the study of urban form, so the research examines the main elements of these towns' form, such as streets, blocks, and public and private spaces. These new towns were consolidated to serve the needs of the countryside, given the importance of agriculture in Mato Grosso's economy. Two points are important for analysis: highways, which in some cases cut through municipalities and fragment the urban fabric, creating distinct urban spaces with distinct territorialities; and the boundaries between urban space and farmland. It is therefore necessary to identify which municipalities have these specific conditions, to check whether these towns offer good conditions for social development and social relations. The research thus analyzes the new Mato Grosso towns whose urban fabric is fragmented by highways and that border farmland, to establish conjectures about their urban morphology and their potential for urban and social development, serving as an analytical tool for future planning.
d.As condições habitacionais da população: Housing conditions are one of the aspects that reveal the many dimensions of social inequality, so improving quality of life is intrinsically linked to better housing conditions. Given the lack of studies on the characteristics of housing in Mato Grosso and Cuiabá and their relationship with residents' social, racial and economic circumstances, this research project relates these variables using data from IBGE's Continuous National Household Sample Survey (PNADc), processed in R, to identify possible socioeconomic weaknesses and support future projects and decisions in the sector.
d.Atualmente, os rios perderam a importânc: Today, rivers have lost their importance in urban life and no longer take part in social activities and urban connections, increasing environmental degradation, pollution and the loss of history. Though important to the development of society, they have become unsuitable, degraded and informally occupied places. Riverside communities, who make their living from the water, are badly harmed by pollution and by the lack of policies to restore and preserve rivers and their surroundings. In Brazil, there have been few public incentives for water restoration and preservation. It is necessary to understand the historical and current relationships between rivers and cities, their continuities and ruptures, with emphasis on the connection of the urban fabric, so that policies to restore and preserve water resources for leisure and daily use can be created. Rivers must again become an integral part of cities and regain their lost social, environmental, historical and cultural values, providing organized and harmonious spaces between the urban and the natural, especially as leisure spaces associated with quality of life. Validity: ordinance 727/2020, 30/05/2020 to 29/05/2021; ordinance 730/2021, 30/05/2021 to 29/05/2022.
d.Considerando que campo de investigação d: Since the production of urban space is an undeniably broad and complex field, this project seeks to understand the processes of appropriation and the cultural representations of the water landscape in Cuiabá-MT. It will inventory the city's water landscape, examine how the territory was appropriated, considering social, economic, cultural and environmental impacts, and analyze how cultural representations of the water landscape materialize in Cuiabá, in order to contribute to ecosystem balance, especially by easing urban problems such as heat islands and air pollution, preventing natural disasters, helping recharge aquifers and contributing to water production in quality and quantity.
d.Desvendar as relações de poder do corone: To uncover the power relations of coronelismo and their influence on urban infrastructure, especially water supply systems, in the municipality of Bauru, from 1896 to 1940. Starting from the hypothesis that the colonels' political, economic and social actions served their own interests at the expense of the population, the work studies: 1) the dialogue between power, the colonel elite and infrastructure; 2) the relationship between political actions and water and sewage services, with special attention to public works; 3) the relations among the agents involved: the urban population, technicians (engineers and other professionals), the colonels and other public authorities regarding urban beautification and development; 4) how the railway took part in implementing water systems and its relationship with the elite and local power. The interest lies in understanding how public policies served the colonels' efforts to control power, urban growth and its infrastructure. The work is expected to contribute to understanding Bauru's urban history through the relationship between public policy and the power of the ruling elite, and to broaden understanding of how water infrastructure was produced.
d.Diante do mau estado de conservação dos: Given the poor state of the buildings and of the documentation (reports, projects, drawings, plans and more), which may be lost over time, and the lack of documentary bases and studies demonstrating the importance of the cultural heritage of the Estrada de Ferro Noroeste do Brasil (EFNOB) railway, this research is proposed under the Fapesp/Condephaat call, to be carried out by researchers of the Architecture: Theory and Projects Research Group (GA). Objectives: to inventory, identify, locate, select and analyze the cultural heritage of the former EFNOB, headquartered in Bauru, kilometer zero of the railway. We intend to research the history of the buildings in relation to the railway and to survey the Central Station, Offices, Workshop Complex and Workers' Village Complex. As complementary work, a historical survey will be made of the recreation and cultural facilities created by the railway in the city, and of how work was organized in the EFNOB offices. The information will be processed and digitized at the EFNOB Railway Industrial Heritage Memory and Virtual Information Center, also to be created by the Project.
d.Esse projeto pretende reproduzir em mode: This project aims to reproduce the historic buildings of downtown Cuiabá as digital models using photogrammetry. The process stores specific building information such as dimensions, textures and details. Photogrammetry has been widely used to represent heritage since digital resources became accessible. Information stored in a digital model can be shared more easily and used in several disciplines involving heritage, history, urbanism and building technology, and is also an important source for possible future restoration of these properties. Photogrammetric models consist of point clouds and mesh structures (digital data of a geometric model made of vertices, edges and faces), which can be produced with the DSM (Dense Stereo Matching) technique using commercial, free or open-source software; this project intends to do all activities with free and open-source software. Likewise, it intends to use mobile phones to take the photographs, making the activities accessible to the academic community.
d.Esta pesquisa investiga criticamente o c: This research critically examines the concept of smart and sustainable cities, questioning its effectiveness as a model of urban development. Although widely promoted as a solution to contemporary urban challenges, these cities often operate within a market logic that favors technological innovation and operational efficiency over socio-spatial equity. The research analyzes how digital infrastructure and environmental policies, instead of democratizing access to the city, can deepen inequalities, reinforce exclusion and consolidate a corporate urbanism serving large investors. It also discusses the contradictions between the rhetoric of sustainability and urban practices that ignore local socioeconomic realities. Using an interdisciplinary approach, the study examines to what extent smart cities are actually sustainable or merely a reconfiguration of urban planning under new technological guidelines. The results aim to contribute to the debate on fairer urban policies that prioritize the right to the city and social inclusion in the face of the digitalization and financialization of urban space.
d.Esta pesquisa pressupõe que o desenvolvi: This research assumes that developing a methodology for a detailed assessment of cities' climate conditions, one that brings these issues into the decision-making process of urban legislation, can help ensure broader and more informed participation of the agents involved. On this basis, it should be possible to establish parameters, proposals and guidelines for producing climate-appropriate urban spaces, ensuring their agreed and continuous application. The general objective is to validate the methodology proposed by Sanches (2015) over time, in three-year application intervals, and to develop a way of assessing wind dynamics within cities, adding another aspect to the discussion. Sanches' (2015) methodology identifies the climate characteristics relevant to urban planning in Sinop, northern Mato Grosso, in a continental equatorial climate with a defined dry season, incorporating the observed urban microclimates and their formation and showing their harmful effects on the community. Ordinance 46/2020, 01/05/2020 to 30/04/2021.
d.Esta pesquisa propõe analisar a segregaç: This research analyzes social and spatial segregation in the Cuiabá–Várzea Grande conurbation, considering the actions of social agents, the logic of the real estate market and the financial system, as well as recent real estate investment promoted by the Growth Acceleration Program (PAC) through the social housing program "Minha Casa Minha Vida". As a result of urbanization marked by high socio-spatial inequality, precarious settlements have reached alarming proportions, especially in Brazilian metropolitan regions, with harmful occupation of environmentally vulnerable areas that are protected by law because of their geophysical fragility. The research will analyze the urbanization of the Cuiabá–Várzea Grande conurbation, in Mato Grosso's metropolitan region, considering the socioeconomic factors of socio-spatial segregation, the housing deficit, environmental degradation and widespread informal access to urban land, to support public policies that improve the population's quality of life.
d.Esta pesquisa propõe uma análise crítica: This research offers a critical analysis of socio-spatial segregation in Brazilian metropolitan regions, showing the structuring role of social agents, the real estate market and the financial system in maintaining urban inequality. Public housing policies, far from truly democratizing access to housing, often reinforce peripheralization and territorial fragmentation, moving vulnerable populations to distant areas without adequate infrastructure. The growth of precarious settlements is not simply a consequence of rapid urbanization, but the result of an exclusionary model of urban development that expels the poorest from consolidated areas and pushes them into environmentally fragile territories, protected by law but systematically disregarded due to land speculation and public neglect. The research therefore problematizes unequal access to urban land and its socio-environmental implications, investigating the housing deficit, environmental degradation and the consolidation of exclusionary urbanism. The analysis aims to support public policies that break with unequal urbanization and promote fairer, more sustainable urban planning able to tackle the structural roots of socio-spatial segregation.
d.Esta pesquisa retoma a discussão sobre a: This research revisits the importance of APPs (permanent preservation areas) for maintaining environmental quality in water source areas, in light of the extreme weather events recently recorded in urban areas. Fundamentally, protecting APPs stems from understanding them as a natural component in the production of ecosystem services, essential to life in all its dimensions and timescales. Despite the relevance of managing environmentally fragile areas in city planning, many problems persist: worsening water pollution, densification and growth of irregular and precarious settlements in fragile areas, and rising socio-environmental vulnerability, among others. In this context, the study highlights the importance of understanding the dynamics of the different functions performed by APPs in cities of the Mato Grosso Cerrado, especially in the metropolitan region of the Cuiabá River Valley. The results may broaden academic debate and show the importance of incorporating APPs into planning and management, considering the geophysical specificities of environmentally and socially fragile areas locally and regionally.
d.Esta pesquisa voltada ao Programa de Pós: This research, part of the Graduate Program in Architecture and Urbanism at FAAC/UNESP (Theory, History and Design), studies the formation of cities from religious heritage and the layout of railways, with emphasis on western São Paulo, continuing the study of São Paulo urban formations created in the second half of the 19th century and their close relationship with coffee and the railway. Within this project, the ongoing research "Estrada de Ferro da Noroeste do Brasil / Bauru, km 0 (EFNOB/Bauru-km 0)" focuses on the EFNOB architectural complex in Bauru and its intrinsic role in the city's urban development. It falls under the FAPESP-SEC/CONDEPHAAT call (FAPESP process 11/51014-6R and CONDEPHAAT 2012/50041-2), whose objectives are to inventory, identify, locate, select, analyze and propose guidelines for safeguarding the cultural heritage of the former Estrada de Ferro Noroeste do Brasil (EFNOB), headquartered in Bauru, kilometer zero of the railway. It will research the history of EFNOB buildings, including the Central Station, train shed and platforms, the Offices and Welfare Department buildings, the Workshops and Roundhouse complex and the Workers' Village, and how work was organized in the EFNOB offices. It will also focus on the railway's direct relationship with city space through the creation of recreation and cultural spaces. Information on EFNOB gathered from governmental and non-governmental institutions will be processed and digitized at the NOB Railway Industrial Heritage Memory and Information Center.
d.Esta proposta de pesquisa dá continuidad: This research proposal continues work begun under FAPEMAT call 02/2008, which resulted in a doctoral thesis on the subject. Its purpose is to investigate how the new planned towns in the interior of Mato Grosso were established from 1970 onwards along the BR-163 highway, which integrates the state by linking Cuiabá-MT to Santarém-PA. The towns analyzed will be Guarantã do Norte, Peixoto de Azevedo, Terra Nova do Norte, Nova Santa Helena, Itaúba and Nova Mutum, completing the sequence of new towns along the highway. The original plans and their expansion will be surveyed and analyzed, considering the possibility of the highway acting as an element of urban dispersal. Building road complexes in the interior of Mato Grosso was seen as support for urban expansion and for strengthening a "model" of town that multiplies and ensures the continued occupation and development of a state long stigmatized as cut off from the rest of Brazil. The highway thus clearly influences the emergence and layout of these towns. In Brazil, the first half of the 1950s was marked by upheaval after President Getúlio Vargas's suicide and moves to prevent the constitutional inauguration of President-elect Juscelino Kubitschek de Oliveira, who, once the crisis was over, pursued his Plan of Goals. In construction and architecture there was an "intensification of differentiation in the construction sector, based mainly on infrastructure, transport, communication, roads and others, in a political-economic project of national integration, building a dynamic and concentrated branch in the sector linked to the most dynamic sectors of the economy" (OSEKI, 1982, p.120, apud SEGAWA, 2005). National integration and modernization spread to new, hitherto unexplored geographic areas. Several settlements were founded in the 1970s in northern Mato Grosso, centered on Alta Floresta, and little is known about their urban "lives". Some questions guide the research: What are these towns like, created mostly in territory empty of people? What remains of the experience of creating many towns and capitals in Brazil? What form do they take years after being founded and faced with the need to grow? What recommendations follow from a technical analysis of how their initial plan unfolded? In studies of towns created in Brazil after 1950, all the emphasis is on Brasília; many other settlements were founded, but little work exists on what became of them. The work will therefore start from an understanding of morphology, plans and projects, with technical and socio-political-economic content for dealing with urban problems. Infrastructure, especially highways, which induce the formation of towns, promotes dispersal and fragmentation of the urban fabric when incorporated into its perimeter. To understand the history, dynamics and systemic change of these planned towns along the BR-163, the research will examine their possible fragmentation and loss of unity due to their proximity to the highway.
d.Este projeto tem como objetivo, analisar: This project analyzes urban morphology from a climate perspective; the different climate behaviors of urban structures are very important for urban climate analysis, especially to support urban planning decisions. Climate-based urban planning should therefore identify and include natural climate variations, seasonal patterns, land use, physical properties (urban geometry and land cover), thermal and radiative properties, management instruments and the valuation of ecosystem services. To this end, it uses Local Climate Zone (LCZ) mapping, a classification proposed by Stewart and Oke (2012) for urban climate studies, which details climate responses in different urban structures, considering built and land cover types.
d.Nas últimas décadas, o desenvolvimento g: In recent decades, the graphic development of computers, which became more affordable, and the spread of information over the internet have produced a profusion of resources for the digital representation of architecture and urbanism. This project integrates different digital resources in a proposal to identify and digitally reproduce the historic urban and architectural site of Barra do Bugres. Through teaching and learning, it explores activities that make it possible to preserve, in digital form, the oldest buildings still standing in the municipality. The planned practices use various digital resources that can broaden students' repertoire and open perspectives for consolidating and continuing their training. Using diverse digital resources in varied activities can develop students' creativity and encourage new uses of technology in architectural representation. The project draws on authors who explore new digital resources for teaching and research in Architecture and Urbanism, such as Kowaltowski (2000), Kolarevic (2003) and Groetelaars (2012).
d.No Brasil a maioria dos municípios tem d: In Brazil, most municipalities struggle to implement territorial planning due to a lack of structure, financial resources and operational conditions. However, geotechnologies, whether paid or free, allow municipalities to develop techniques and applications using spatial data to obtain basic references and analyze the built space as a whole (AKAISHI, 2011). Any action to order or monitor urban space must be part of an analytical process that integrates the different components of the system, physical, biotic and human occupation, with a view to planning and managing the territory (MORETTI, 2011). To speed up territorial planning based on physical, environmental, economic and social characteristics, geotechnology tools offer greater speed and versatility and allow information to be shared more cheaply and quickly. With this focus, the research presents new methodological procedures using geoprocessing (GIS) tools that can make up for the lack of geographic, socioeconomic and environmental data, specifically in decision-making. Its general objective is to apply geotechnologies to spatial analysis for territorial planning and ordering in the metropolitan region of the Cuiabá River Valley.
d.O Núcleo de Estudos das Espacialidades C: The Center for Studies of Contemporary Spatialities (NEC, IAU-USP) deals with the spatial, cultural and artistic transformations that have characterized the contemporary world through the interrelations between architecture, art, city and society. Understanding that, beyond regulating the productive order, contemporary space merges productive mechanisms and symbolic projections into a hybrid space that requires new means of conceptual and phenomenal apprehension, it seeks to formulate analytical processes and methodologies suited to this new object, and to characterize new sensibilities and their potential to intervene in the social processes that shape individual and collective existence. The center originated in 2006 in what was then the Department of Architecture and Urbanism, now the Institute of Architecture and Urbanism (IAU), of USP's São Carlos campus, and was registered in the CNPq Directory of Research Groups in 2007.
d.O Plano Diretor Municipal (PDM) é um ins: The Municipal Master Plan (PDM) is an instrument of Federal Law 10.257/2001, which establishes the City Statute and sets public-order and social-interest rules regulating the use of urban property in defense of the common good, safety, citizens' well-being and sustainability. Under this law, the PDM is the basic instrument of urban expansion policy and must be revised at least every ten years, or whenever the public administration deems it necessary. Applying the concepts of smart and sustainable cities is a way to solve many problems caused by rapid urbanization. Since urban planning is a means of applying these concepts, the Master Plan is a key instrument in developing smart, connected cities. This work addresses the urban surveys of Tangará da Serra to produce diagnoses as a tool for understanding the urban territory and offering alternatives for its sustainable and smart expansion. It involves research to produce urban maps of land use and occupation, urban expansion, and areas of environmental and housing interest, and to identify relevant elements that may fragment or restructure the urban fabric, as well as historic elements, in order to read and profile the city and support diagnoses and proposals.
d.O avanço da fronteira agrícola de Mato G: The northward advance of Mato Grosso's agricultural frontier, seeking an export route for commodities via the Pacific Ocean, was designed through the Center-North Corridor, formed by the BR-163 and BR-230 (Trans-Amazonian) highways and the Tapajós and Amazon rivers. The route, which starts in northern Mato Grosso, crosses Pará and ends at the port of Santana, in Macapá (AP), saves more than 5,000 km compared with the BR-163 route used to carry commodities to ports in the South and Southeast. The research seeks to identify likely changes brought by the project, given the prospect of geographic, socioeconomic and ecological change, and at the same time to decode the threats to the daily life and traditional cultures of indigenous peoples along the new route in the Legal Amazon.
d.O consumo excessivo de recursos naturais: Excessive consumption of natural resources has intensified the search for new alternative materials that reduce the environmental burden of materials commonly used in construction, preferably cementitious materials with mechanical properties equal or superior to conventional ones. This project will develop three sets of cementitious mortar composites: (1) replacing drinking water by volume with 25, 50 and 100% sugarcane vinasse; (2) replacing natural sand by volume with 25, 50 and 100% waste foundry sand (WFS); and (3) a third set with the optimized mix of both residues. A special concrete, interlocking paving for light traffic, will then be developed. The residues will first be characterized using structural techniques (FT-IR/ATR, XRF and XRD) and, for vinasse only, physicochemical characterization of pH, reducing sugars (RS), total reducing sugars (TRS), and chemical and biochemical oxygen demand (COD and BOD). The physical-mechanical properties of the alternative composites will be analyzed according to international standards (ASTM): setting time and consistency in the fresh state, and density, water absorption, void ratio, three-point bending and compression in the hardened state. Depending on the results, the material will be patented and directed to applications.
d.O desenho urbano e a adoção de medidas d: Urban design and situational crime prevention measures, by influencing spatial configurations and aspects of people's daily lives, can help encourage or inhibit certain crimes, especially crimes of opportunity such as residential burglary, depending on how they are adopted. This research studies residential burglaries in Cuiabá to analyze how the distribution of these crimes in certain neighborhoods relates to their spatial configuration and to residents' use of situational crime prevention measures, which may inform public policy on urban planning and public safety. It adopts a multi-method approach based mainly on statistical document analysis and case studies, using georeferenced mapping, site visits and interviews with residents and offenders. The expected result is an overview of where burglaries occur in Cuiabá and of the relationship between urban design and situational prevention features that may be encouraging or inhibiting residential burglaries in certain neighborhoods.
d.O grupo tem como objetivo realizar pesqu: The group aims to carry out research that draws broadly on the concept of the "right to the city" and its implications for socio-spatial dynamics, recognizing the hybrid nature of contemporary space, where productive mechanisms intertwine with symbolic projections. It seeks to formulate analytical processes and methodologies to understand the social movements that organize to appropriate urban space and for social and territorial transformation. It addresses demands for housing, land, public transport, open public spaces and urban space as a space of lived experience and symbolic production, showing how a new form of urban poverty affects the inhabitants of contemporary cities. It seeks to understand how these demands are resolved in tension with the reproduction of capital and power, by investigating processes of appropriation of urban space. This means considering the regulatory role of the State and the role of social movements, culture and cultural policies, and how they affect the economic and social development of cities.
d.O objetivo da pesquisa é compreender a r: The aim of the research is to understand the relationship between the territorial formation of Mato Grosso and the production of its landscapes as cultural representation, understanding sociocultural correlations and new ways of occupying the city. It studies the occupation of the state's territory and the shaping of its networks of cities, presenting the singularities and pluralities of the landscapes produced. Tangible and intangible heritage, memory, infrastructure and works of art will be the keys to reading the landscape as cultural representation, studying the relationship between the history of cities and the territory. Theoretical and empirical procedures are proposed. Theoretically, the research will review authors who discuss its themes, such as territory, landscape, culture, sociocultural relations, heritage and memory, infrastructure systems, urbanization and knowledge. Historical documents are of great value: documentary research will cover period newspapers, city council minutes, municipal ordinances, city hall documents and reports, iconographic material (photos, images, old postcards, etc.) and maps. Empirically, it will be based on fieldwork and cross-referencing of data and content. Critical reading of the literature and primary sources, together with analysis of cartography, maps, plans, photographs and other iconographic documents, will connect materials and methods in the research produced by this project. A theoretical/historiographic and bibliographic method will be used, with primary and secondary sources for the conceptual part, as well as an analytical and descriptive method for specific case studies, assessing divergences and convergences in the production of landscapes as cultural representation. Understanding landscape as cultural occupation is necessary to understand social relations in the territory and to recover inhabitants' memory and the technical know-how applied in architecture and landscape, so as to rethink sociocultural correlations and new ways of occupying the city. The intention is to bring new elements to the debate in urbanism and culture, presenting different scales of intervention, since its object is the landscape. It will foster the exchange of scientific knowledge among peers. The results will serve as decision-making tools, which public authorities may use to reinterpret and produce urban space and as parameters for heritage and cultural policies in the state.
d.O objetivo desta pesquisa é o de analisa: The aim of this research is to analyze to what extent higher education institutions in the Baixada Cuiabana region of Mato Grosso prepare graduates of their in-person Architecture and Urbanism programs to use the BIM methodology. The specific objectives are: 1. to identify the courses in which BIM is or could be used by institutions offering Architecture and Urbanism degrees in the region; 2. to identify whether the institutions have the technology, laboratories, software and trained faculty needed to use this methodology. It is thus expected to identify the skills graduates acquire through the use of BIM during their studies.
d.O objetivo principal do Grupo de Estudos: The main aim of the Study Group is to discuss concepts and approaches to Landscape. For Assunto (1973), landscape is the unity of history and nature: nature that takes shape by assimilating the history that molds it; history that, identifying itself in nature, becomes the content of the forms it gave to nature. The landscape approach is complex, since a landscape can never be defined by a single element; its elements are always changing, just as human experiences in space are constantly evolving. However, there is no consensus among researchers on the definition of landscape. Besse (2006) explains the term's many meanings by the fact that many academic disciplines study landscape, each starting from its own theoretical references and reaching different approaches. What is becoming consensus is that landscape cannot be defined only as "what one sees" (a scene) or only as the physical elements of a spatial area. Besse (2006) proposes five possible entries for landscape issues: landscape as cultural representation, as territory produced by societies over history, as a systemic complex linking natural and cultural elements, as a space of sensory and subjective experience, and as a design context. Meinig (1979) also admits that the central problem in studying landscape is to think of it not only as what the eyes see but also as a mental construction. He argues that there are many ways of "seeing the same scene", as many interpretations as there are observers, and proposes ten ways of seeing a landscape: as nature, habitat, system, problem, wealth, ideology, history, place and aesthetics. Each of these "ways of seeing" suggests a type of approach, a different aspect of the same reality.
d.O presente projeto de extensão parte da: This extension project starts from the premise that the built environment influences many activities. Considering the teaching workplace, and aiming to create a space of belonging and creativity, a call will select the team with the most suitable and creative proposal, based on guiding words, for an artistic intervention on the wall of the campus staff room. The method has three stages: preparing and publicizing an open call that allows participation by the wider community; selecting the team with the most suitable proposal; and the team's execution of the intervention. Expected results include bringing the wider community closer to IFMT-VGD and letting it get to know the campus, and creating a space designed for teachers' activities where, through a sense of belonging, they spend more time, fostering relations among colleagues and interdisciplinary work.
d.O presente projeto de extensão será dese: This extension project will be carried out in line with the State Environmental Education Policy. Its objectives are to develop formal and informal environmental education with schools and the community of the Jacaré micro-basin (Várzea Grande), to diagnose sanitation and health conditions around Jacaré Lagoon, to create an Association and to prepare an architectural design for the Lagoon Park. It also continues the environmental education project at Ernandy M. Baracat State School in Várzea Grande (MT). The project has four components: 1) Educational: continuing and strengthening the environmental education project at Ernandy Baracat school and extending it to five more neighboring public schools in the Jacaré micro-basin, based on the VERAH method, through teacher training courses. The VERAH method (Vegetation, Erosion, Waste, Water, Housing) of interdisciplinary inquiry and teaching involves a participatory diagnosis of the environmental quality of the micro-basin where the school and its community are located; 2) Social mobilization: environmental education with the community living in the micro-basin, including students and their families, through the creation of an Association; 3) Research: technical studies of drainage, the location and volume of sewage discharged into the lagoon, topography, hydrology and endemic diseases around Jacaré Lagoon, to support the architectural design of the Jacaré Lagoon Park, a community aspiration; 4) Urban intervention: preparing the architectural design of the Jacaré Lagoon Park, based on the studies in the three components above and after consulting the community and schools. The project will be carried out in partnership with UNIVAG (Centro Universitário de Várzea Grande) and CEFAPRO (Mato Grosso's Center for the Training and Updating of Basic Education Professionals, part of SEDUC-MT). The outputs will be scientific articles, an e-book and a diagnostic dossier on Jacaré Lagoon to obtain public funding for building the Lagoon Park.
d.O presente projeto de pesquisa parte da: This research project starts from the IPCC (2018) definition of climate change: a change in the state of the climate that can be identified by changes in the mean and/or variability of its properties and that persists for an extended period, whether due to natural internal processes, natural external forcings or persistent anthropogenic changes in atmospheric composition and land use. Climate change poses significant challenges for urban planning worldwide, affecting inhabitants' well-being and quality of life; as air temperatures rise due to more impermeable, low-reflectance urban materials, cities will experience the urban heat island effect, leading to higher energy consumption, harm to human health and greater environmental impacts. The research will examine future climate change scenarios through projections of mean air temperature for the Metropolitan Region of the Cuiabá River Valley for 2021-2040, 2041-2060, 2061-2080 and 2081-2100 using the CNRM-ESM2-1 model and the SSP3-7.0 scenario, and will assess the future climate relationship with today's urbanization process.
d.O presente projeto pretende documentar,: This project aims to document, analyze and discuss the cultural value of architectural works, events and/or urban interventions, from the colonial period to 20th-century modern production, that give identity and distinction to Brazil's main cities, especially Cuiabá and Várzea Grande and, more broadly, the other cities of Mato Grosso. Brazilian cities bring together a wide range of buildings and urban experiences from different periods and influences, forming a unique cultural mosaic. As a result, many professionals find it hard not only to distinguish and classify them by their formal and spatial characteristics, but above all to deal with and take into account the identity of each place.
d.O projeto \"Dinâmicas Culturais e Socioa: The project "Dinâmicas Culturais e Socioambientais na Paisagem Hídrica Urbana de Cuiabá: Um Estudo de Caso Iconográfico" seeks to understand the cultural appropriations and representations of the water landscape in Cuiabá, Mato Grosso. Based on an iconographic approach, it analyzes how the urban landscape is shaped by social, economic and environmental processes, using images and visual symbols to interpret its transformations and meanings. It is an empirical case study conducted between April 2024 and March 2025 at UNIVAG – Centro Universitário de Várzea Grande/MT. The method includes a literature review, field trips to collect iconographic data, and qualitative and quantitative analysis of visual records. The central aim is to investigate how the water landscape is appropriated and represented, deepening understanding of the interactions between urbanization and the environment. It is justified by the need to discuss the impacts of urbanization on permanent preservation areas, considering their effects on environmental quality and sustainable urban planning. The study seeks to support more effective public policies for managing water landscapes, balancing development and environmental conservation.
d.O projeto \"Áreas Verdes Públicas: Avali: The project "Áreas Verdes Públicas: Avaliação e Valorização no Contexto de Cuiabá e Várzea Grande MT" investigates the importance of urban green spaces for environmental quality and people's quality of life. Grounded in Architecture and Urbanism, it uses a qualitative and quantitative approach to analyze the distribution, infrastructure and public perception of green areas in the Cuiabá–Várzea Grande conurbation. It is justified by rapid urban growth and the shortage of accessible green areas, which are essential for urban sustainability and social well-being. Research shows that these spaces help regulate climate, reduce pollution and provide thermal comfort, as well as fostering social cohesion and leisure. The method involves mapping and categorizing green areas, surveying available infrastructure, analyzing maintenance and accessibility, and using interviews and questionnaires to understand users' perceptions. Environmental data will also be collected to assess these spaces' contribution to mitigating urban impacts. Expected results include a detailed diagnosis of urban green areas and recommendations for public policies that value and preserve these spaces, essential to urban quality of life.
d.O projeto de extensão \"Cidades + Verdes: The central aim of the "Cidades + Verdes" extension project is to raise awareness among early primary school children (ages 4 and 5) of the importance of urban green areas such as squares, gardens and parks, and to value the vegetation of the regional biomes, especially the Cerrado, Pantanal and Amazon. Through an educational approach, it seeks to show new generations the key role of these spaces in environmental balance and quality of life in cities. Developed by faculty and students of the City, Society and Landscape Research Group of UNIVAG's Stricto Sensu Graduate Program in Architecture and Urbanism (PPGAU-UNIVAG), in association with PUC Campinas, the project will be carried out in public schools in Várzea Grande, Mato Grosso. Activities include age-appropriate talks using accessible language, audiovisual resources, illustrations and short videos to aid understanding and engagement. The talks will highlight the importance of native vegetation of the regional biomes, focusing on the environmental and social benefits of urban green areas, such as temperature regulation, better air quality and encouraging social interaction. Afterwards, an informative newspaper with educational content on urban green areas and their vegetation will be handed out; children can take it home, extending the project's reach to their families. Follow-up activities such as question-and-answer sessions will be held, and practical actions will be suggested to teachers, such as visits to local parks and native tree planting projects. The project is justified by the growing urbanization of Várzea Grande, where the lack of urban green areas affects quality of life and the environment. It thus aims to foster respect and care for the environment, contribute to early environmental education, promote the preservation of urban green spaces and strengthen the relationship between society and nature.
d.O projeto de extensão Cuiabá e o Direito: The extension project "Cuiabá e o Direito à cidade: da teoria à educação em quadrinhos", linked to the Graduate Program in Architecture and Urbanism of Centro Universitário de Várzea Grande (UNIVAG), promotes critical reflection on the Right to the City and its social and environmental implications, using comics as a teaching resource. The concept of the Right to the City, coined by philosopher Henri Lefebvre, is a human and collective right that defends urban space as a common good, opposing the commodification of territories and proposing a city that is inclusive and accessible to all. The project has three stages. The first, "David Harvey and the problem of (urban) space and Capital", took place from May to July 2024, with meetings to read and discuss texts by geographer David Harvey, providing a theoretical basis for the rest of the project. In the second, "Cuiabá in Comics: A Contemporary View of the Right to the City", undergraduate Architecture and Urbanism students at UNIVAG, trained in creative and drawing techniques, are developing a comic, from character development to scripting and digital finishing. The story addresses contemporary urban and environmental issues in Cuiabá, focusing on the Right to the City. One of the main characters is a grandmother from Cuiabá, created with local features such as expressions of local speech, to value local knowledge; she represents the importance of a critical perspective that links environmental and urban issues to popular wisdom. The third stage, "Right to the City in Practice: Educating with Comics", consists of workshops with public school students using the material as a teaching resource, making it possible to assess students' understanding and engagement and promoting critical awareness of Cuiabá's contemporary urban challenges.
d.O projeto investiga a lacuna entre o que: The project investigates the gap between what Municipal Master Plans (PDMs) provide for and what is actually implemented in practice, known as the policy-implementation gap. It assumes that many PDMs include innovation and sustainability guidelines without translating them into verifiable operational provisions such as targets, instruments, governance, funding and monitoring mechanisms. The study analyzes municipalities that won the Mato Grosso Innovative Cities Award, examining whether and how this award acts as a mechanism to induce the implementation of urban policies. Methodologically, it takes a qualitative approach, with comparative document analysis of the PDMs and the award documents, supported by a structured protocol for assessing regulatory implementability. As a contribution, the project proposes a replicable model for measuring the policy gap, along with recommendations to improve both Master Plans and policy-inducing mechanisms, reducing the distance between regulatory guidelines and actual implementation capacity at the municipal level.
d.O projeto tem como objetivo analisar as: The project analyzes conditions for active mobility (walking and cycling) in cities of Mato Grosso, focusing on urban infrastructure, road safety, accessibility, social inclusion and sustainability. It uses technical-participatory diagnostic methods, field data collection, analysis of local public policies and geospatial tools to map and assess the urban network. It seeks to identify barriers to and potential for encouraging active mobility, supporting intervention and urban planning proposals for more inclusive, resilient and sustainable cities. The project also considers the interface between mobility, public health and socio-environmental justice, with emphasis on vulnerable populations.
d.O trabalho dá continuidade a projeto já: The work continues a previous project that catalogued existing buildings in Barra do Bugres built with adobe. It aims to revive the raw earth building technique of adobe by training workers to spread a vernacular, sustainable material that requires no special skills and allows community self-building. Adobe was also part of the earliest buildings when Barra do Bugres was founded. In addition, sugarcane bagasse and ash, abundant in the region due to extensive sugar and ethanol production, will be used as aggregate in the adobe mix. Courses and workshops will be offered on soil characterization and brick making.
d.Projeto para reforma do prédio extremame: Project for the renovation of a severely damaged building housing a meeting center for the elderly, which had already been approved for funding from the city of Cuiabá but could not receive it for lack of a design. Our team surveyed the site and the areas where an enclosed function hall is planned, where films and online talks can be shown, while also enlarging the space already used for handicraft classes and social gatherings. Besides spaces for leisure and weekly meetings, the project includes bathrooms, a kitchen and a service room. Since the property belongs to the group leader's grandmother, there is interest in improving conditions without the risk of having to rent out or sell the property once renovated.
d.Tem como objetivo observar o comportamen: Its aim is to observe the behavior of the heat island in Cuiabá-MT in 2011/2012, 2016 and 2019/2020, together with land cover data and their relationship with municipal planning indices, and to test urban planning indicators based on the findings by simulating future scenarios. To do so, the following steps are needed: a) collecting air temperature, relative humidity and land cover classification data along transects; b) surveying building heights along the route, then comparing and analyzing the data across years against municipal planning indices; c) testing urban planning indicators based on the findings; d) simulating future scenarios from the best results.
